analysis.investment_thesis: DOMS is a genuinely excellent business — ROCE of 26.2%, net profit CAGR of 41.3% over 5 years, and a dominant consumer brand in Indian stationery — but it is priced like a luxury good at EV/EBITDA of 39.3x and earnings yield of only ~2.4% (EBIT INR 349 Cr / EV ~INR 14,669 Cr). The Magic Formula rewards both quality AND cheapness; DOMS only delivers one of the two.
key_strengths: ROCE of 26.2% (above my 25% 'excellent' threshold) and ROE of 22.3% confirm this is a genuinely high-quality capital allocator with real competitive advantages in the Indian education stationery market
Operating income CAGR of 35.6% and net profit CAGR of 41.3% over 5 years are exceptional — this is a business that is scaling with improving margins, not deteriorating ones
Low leverage (D/E 0.14) with strong promoter ownership (70.38%) — management has skin in the game and a clean balance sheet to fund growth organically
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~2.4% (EBIT INR 349 Cr on EV of ~INR 14,669 Cr) is 5x below my minimum threshold — the stock is pricing in a decade of perfect execution and there is zero margin of safety

FCF is barely positive or negative despite strong earnings (INR –26 Cr in FY25, INR 29 Cr in FY24) as capex accelerates to INR 213 Cr — high capex intensity (61% of EBITDA) reduces real FCF yield substantially
Revenue base is still small (INR 1,913 Cr in FY25); the company is moving into baby diapers/wet wipes — diversification away from core stationery introduces execution risk and capital dilution
red_flags: P/E of 65.4x and EV/EBITDA of 39.3x embed extraordinary growth assumptions — any slowdown in the 35-40% earnings CAGR would cause severe multiple contraction from these levels
CWIP jumped from INR 25 Cr (FY24) to INR 101 Cr (FY25), and capex nearly doubled to INR 213 Cr — returns on this new capital investment are unproven and could dilute the excellent historical ROCE
The stationery market is increasingly competitive with organized and unorganized players; pricing power assumptions embedded in the valuation may be optimistic
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula math: EV = INR 14,517 + 212 – 60 = INR 14,669 Cr. EBIT (Operating Income FY25) = INR 349 Cr. Earnings Yield = 2.38% — the lowest in this cohort alongside Delhivery. However, ROCE = 26.2% is the highest in this group and genuinely excellent. The problem is simple: Magic Formula ranks companies on the combined score of BOTH metrics. A world-class ROCE paired with a near-zero earnings yield produces an average combined rank, not a top-decile one.

I genuinely like the DOMS business — strong brand, improving margins, low debt, owner-operated. This is the kind of company I'd love to own if the market mispriced it. At P/E of 65x, it's priced for perfection. My formula says wait for either (a) a significant price correction that pushes earnings yield above 10%, or (b) earnings to grow so rapidly that the multiple naturally compresses. Neither condition is met today.
